correctness.rationale: For every finite invariant support, the doubling restriction permutes its points. Each prescribed predecessor forces an inverse-branch bit. Disjoint complementary gaps force the corresponding switches; the seam has opposite monodromy so it costs one jump precisely for equal end bits. Moving jumps away from supports, and putting single jumps only in the forced gaps, constructs a matching selector. Modular arithmetic gives the all-fixed-points parity pattern and the exact count \(2^n-1\). Sorted cyclic rotations identify the branch word with the BWT last column. Direct replay of verify.py produced 1,197 exact rational assertions over 315 finite families, including independent local side-label minimization for small instances; tests are not a proof of the general theorem.

value.rationale: For any prescribed finite invariant union, the exact minimum number of petals is a natural dynamical covering invariant. The theorem is a uniform, constructive full classification rather than a parameter-selected example; the complete fixed point set of the n-th iterate forces exactly \(2^n-1\) petals. The BWT identity provides a geometric interpretation of a computable primitive-necklace invariant and makes sharp algebraic-combinatorial constraints available for flower coverings. Its scope is finite and no broader dynamical entropy claim is made.
